title: Things into Which Angels Long to Look
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: The prophets longed to see the age we live in. Don't believe the lie that you were born in the wrong era. Step into God's mission for your time.
exhortation: It struck me as I read this that each of us is given a unique grace, tailored to our time and place. The prophets of old longed to glimpse the era we now live in, but that knowledge wasn't given to them. Instead, God revealed that they were serving not themselves but us, testifying so that those living in the age of Christ would recognize that all history and prophecy pointed to Jesus.

Do you realize that one of the enemy's simple tactics is to make you resent your own era? He wants you to believe you were born in the wrong century, to sigh for the good old days and romanticize whatever age seems coolest: the age of knights, a time of just wars, or small-town nostalgia. We need to stop all that and reject the lie that we are somehow misplaced.

Maybe you feel like Frodo, wishing the ring had never come to him. Maybe, like me sometimes, you lament the age of the internet, where countless evils are available in the palm of your hand and seemingly unspeakable evils are taking over our country and invading our schools. But as Gandalf told Frodo, we don't get to choose the times we live in. We only decide what to do with the time we're given.

We live in the age in which the mysteries of Christ have been revealed. How incredible is that? What do we have to complain about? Whatever else we think, this knowledge of our Lord and Savior makes us, of all people, blessed. We are equipped with gifts and knowledge meant for our time and our age. We hold a unique piece of the story of God's plan and contribute our own verse and chapter to its unfolding. What a gift and what a privilege. Let's step into God's mission this morning.
prayer: Lord, thank you for the times we live in. Open our eyes to the harvest that is ripe around us. There is great work to be done, because you are still working today, and it is because of your grace and patience that you haven't come yet.

Open our eyes to the souls around us who need to hear the truth of the gospel: that you came, so that we don't have to pay for our sin with an eternity separated from you, but can look to you, Jesus, who shed your blood on the cross so that we might be forgiven and live with you forever. These are wonderful times to be living in. Open our eyes, Lord.
